concepts.title: Frequency and Period of Periodic Motion
concepts.definition: Periodic motion repeats at fixed time intervals. The duration of one complete cycle is the period, and the rate of repetitions per unit time is the frequency.
concepts.key_idea: Frequency and time period are inverse quantities measuring the speed of repetition.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: find the frequency and time period when a body completes {count} cycles in {duration} seconds
calculate the oscillation frequency and period for {count} beats per {duration} seconds
what is the frequency and period of a cyclic motion executing {count} repetitions in {duration} seconds
determine the time period and frequency given {count} complete vibrations in {duration} seconds
how much is the time period and frequency if an object oscillates {count} times during {duration} seconds

solution_steps.explain: frequency is total oscillations divided by time taken
period is reciprocal of frequency

solution_steps.action: verify the inverse relationship between frequency and period
solution_steps.explain: confirm that frequency times period equals unity, ensuring consistency of the computed values

concepts.title: Angular Frequency of Oscillatory Motion
concepts.definition: Angular frequency measures the rate of change of phase angle in simple harmonic motion expressed in radians per second.
concepts.key_idea: Angular frequency connects the physical time period to phase rotation speed.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: calculate the angular frequency for an oscillation with time period {T} seconds
find angular frequency omega when period is {T} s
what is the angular frequency of a simple harmonic oscillator having time period {T} seconds
determine angular speed omega given period {T} s
how much is angular frequency for a pendulum with period {T} seconds

solution_steps.explain: angular frequency is 2 pi divided by period T

solution_steps.action: compute the frequency from the angular frequency
solution_steps.explain: frequency equals angular frequency divided by 2 pi, providing the cyclic rate in hertz

solution_steps.action: verify consistency between angular frequency and period
solution_steps.explain: confirm that omega times period equals 2 pi, ensuring the phase completes one full cycle per period

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving angular frequency of oscillatory motion.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate angular frequency. Step 2: compute the frequency from the angular frequency. Step 3: verify consistency between angular frequency and period. Working: (2 * pi) / period, omega / (2 * pi).
worked_examples.answer: Angular Frequency of Oscillatory Motion applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.answer: The method of angular frequency of oscillatory motion leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Maximum Velocity in Simple Harmonic Motion
concepts.definition: Peak speed in simple harmonic motion occurs as the particle passes through its central equilibrium position.
concepts.key_idea: Maximum speed equals angular frequency multiplied by motion amplitude.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: find the maximum speed of a particle in SHM with amplitude {amplitude} and angular frequency {omega}
calculate the peak velocity in simple harmonic motion with amplitude {amplitude} m and angular frequency {omega} rad/s

how much is the highest speed achieved in SHM of amplitude {amplitude} and angular frequency {omega}

solution_steps.explain: peak speed is product of angular frequency and amplitude

solution_steps.action: compute the maximum kinetic energy of the oscillating particle
solution_steps.explain: peak kinetic energy equals half mass times v_max squared, representing total energy at equilibrium

solution_steps.action: verify that maximum speed occurs at the equilibrium position
solution_steps.explain: at equilibrium displacement is zero so all energy is kinetic, confirming v_max is the peak speed

concepts.title: Maximum Acceleration in Simple Harmonic Motion
concepts.definition: Maximum acceleration magnitude occurs at extreme displacement points where restoring force is largest.
concepts.key_idea: Peak acceleration is directly proportional to displacement amplitude and square of angular frequency.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: calculate maximum acceleration for SHM with angular frequency {omega} and amplitude {amplitude}
find peak acceleration in simple harmonic motion given angular frequency {omega} rad/s and amplitude {amplitude} m

determine peak acceleration for an oscillator with amplitude {amplitude} m and angular speed {omega} rad/s
how much is the peak magnitude of acceleration in SHM of amplitude {amplitude} and angular frequency {omega}

solution_steps.explain: acceleration formula depends on square of omega
peak acceleration is omega squared times amplitude

solution_steps.action: verify that maximum acceleration occurs at the extreme displacement
solution_steps.explain: at maximum displacement the restoring force is largest, so acceleration peaks at the amplitude position

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving maximum acceleration in simple harmonic motion.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: square the angular frequency. Step 2: multiply by amplitude. Step 3: verify that maximum acceleration occurs at the extreme displacement. Working: omega ** 2, omega_sq * amplitude.
worked_examples.answer: Maximum Acceleration in Simple Harmonic Motion applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.answer: The method of maximum acceleration in simple harmonic motion leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Oscillation Period of Spring Mass System
concepts.definition: A block connected to a spring executes simple harmonic motion under a linear restoring force with period depending on mass and spring stiffness.
concepts.key_idea: Time period increases with inertia mass and decreases with spring stiffness.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: calculate the time period of oscillation for mass {mass} attached to spring with constant {spring_constant}
find time period of a mass spring oscillator given mass {mass} kg and spring constant {spring_constant} N/m

determine time period of simple harmonic motion for mass {mass} kg and stiffness {spring_constant} N/m
how much time does one oscillation take for mass {mass} connected to spring constant {spring_constant}

solution_steps.explain: ratio gives inertia over stiffness
frequency factor depends on square root of ratio
time period is 2 pi times root ratio

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving oscillation period of spring mass system.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: divide mass by spring constant. Step 2: take square root. Step 3: multiply by 2 pi. Working: mass / spring_constant, sqrt(ratio), 2 * pi * root_val.
worked_examples.answer: Oscillation Period of Spring Mass System applied step by step gives the required result.

concepts.title: Total Mechanical Energy in SHM
concepts.definition: Total mechanical energy in frictionless simple harmonic motion is conserved and proportional to the square of amplitude.
concepts.key_idea: Total energy remains constant throughout oscillation and equals peak potential energy.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: calculate total mechanical energy in SHM with spring constant {spring_constant} and amplitude {amplitude}
find total energy of harmonic oscillator having stiffness {spring_constant} N/m and amplitude {amplitude} m

determine total mechanical energy given spring constant {spring_constant} and amplitude {amplitude}
how much energy is stored in SHM with force constant {spring_constant} and amplitude {amplitude}

solution_steps.explain: energy depends on square of amplitude
total energy is half times spring constant times amplitude squared

solution_steps.action: verify energy conservation by comparing total energy to peak potential energy
solution_steps.explain: at maximum displacement all energy is potential, so total energy equals the peak PE value

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving total mechanical energy in shm.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: square amplitude. Step 2: calculate total energy. Step 3: verify energy conservation by comparing total energy to peak potential energy. Working: amplitude ** 2, 0.5 * spring_constant * amp_sq.
worked_examples.answer: Total Mechanical Energy in SHM applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply total mechanical energy in shm to a fresh example and interpret the result.

worked_examples.answer: The method of total mechanical energy in shm leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Potential Energy at Displacement in SHM
concepts.definition: Potential energy of a linear harmonic oscillator at any displacement from equilibrium depends on displacement squared.
concepts.key_idea: Potential energy varies quadratically with displacement and peaks at extreme positions.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: find potential energy in SHM at displacement {displacement} for spring constant {spring_constant}

solution_steps.explain: potential energy varies with square of displacement
PE is half spring constant times displacement squared

solution_steps.action: compute the corresponding kinetic energy at the given displacement
solution_steps.explain: kinetic energy equals total energy minus potential energy, ensuring energy conservation at any displacement

concepts.title: Time Period of Simple Pendulum
concepts.definition: For small angular swings, a simple pendulum executes simple harmonic motion with time period depending on string length and gravitational acceleration.
concepts.key_idea: Simple pendulum period is independent of bob mass and amplitude for small angular displacements.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: calculate time period of a simple pendulum of length {length} m where gravitational acceleration is {g}

solution_steps.action: divide length by acceleration due to gravity
solution_steps.explain: ratio of length to g determines square of angular time factor
time period depends on square root of length to g ratio
period equals 2 pi times root value

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving time period of simple pendulum.

worked_examples.answer: Time Period of Simple Pendulum applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply time period of simple pendulum to a fresh example and interpret the result.

concepts.title: Length of Simple Pendulum for Given Period
concepts.definition: The required length of a simple pendulum to achieve a specific time period can be computed from gravitational acceleration.
concepts.key_idea: Length of simple pendulum scales directly as square of time period.
question_patterns: in Class 11 physics oscillations: calculate the length of a simple pendulum having time period {period} seconds where g is {g}

solution_steps.explain: length varies with square of period
denominator contains pi squared
4 times pi squared is denominator factor
length equals g times period squared divided by 4 pi squared

worked_examples.solution: Step 1: square period. Step 2: square pi. Step 3: calculate denominator. Step 4: calculate length. Working: period ** 2, pi ** 2, 4 * pi_sq, (g * period_sq) / denom.
worked_examples.answer: Length of Simple Pendulum for Given Period applied step by step gives the required result.

concepts.title: Verification of Simple Harmonic Motion Conditions
concepts.definition: A motion is simple harmonic if restoring force or acceleration is directly proportional to displacement and directed towards the mean position.
concepts.key_idea: Linear dependence of acceleration on negative displacement characterizes simple harmonic motion.
